evidence.text: This character-specific entry analyzes 上 as an indicative graph: a short mark above a reference line indicates the upper side. It reports curved baselines in oracle-bone examples, often straightened in later forms; early oracle-bone and bronze forms could resemble 二, while many late Spring-and-Autumn forms add a vertical stroke to distinguish the graph. It reports Shang inscriptional examples including 上帝 (Heji 16703) and 上甲 (Heji 6384), and Zhou bronze spatial uses. These are the dictionary's reports, not independent artifact inspections.

evidence.text: The character-specific account describes oracle-bone 上 as two horizontal strokes, a longer lower reference line and shorter upper marker. It says the upper stroke appears vertical in later bronze and small-seal forms to distinguish the graph from 二, and a dot appears in the modern standard form. This differs from CUHK's description of curved early baselines; both describe a positional mark above a reference line.

gaps: The inspected paleographic accounts differ on whether early oracle-bone examples have a curved reference line or two horizontal strokes. No primary artifact image was visually inspected to resolve the variation.
The CUHK entry reports Shang and Zhou inscription examples, but this run did not independently inspect the named artifacts.

The alternate Commons file page was inaccessible, so no verified direct image URL or rights evidence is available. The previously supplied Orakelknochen.JPG image URL is excluded because acquisition returned 404. The supplied 上-seal.svg description is a possible existing candidate but was not re-inspected during this invocation; no image is proposed here.

No phonetic or semantic components are proposed; sources analyze 上 as an indicative graph. No dated semantic sequence was established for extensions such as ‘superior’, ‘ruler’ or verbal ‘ascend/send up’.
The upstream Unicode individual-character lookup and local reading rows were not independently verified during this web pass.
